label: 978-r1
verdict: fixed but misses its mark on the serving path
verdict_basis: Correctness: the corrected 0793 fixes candidate-55's boot failure (NameError in AsyncLLM.__init__ on every tp4-ring boot) and the 13 release-test failures; tests/v1/engine and tests/entrypoints/serve/utils now fail exactly where candidate-54 fails (environmental), with 11 new cases passing.

Own mark as declared (the PR's bench_mm_prefix_fastpath.py, ABBA against candidate-54, 2 boots each): met. Turn-2+ host time is faster beyond the interval in 8 of 8 workloads (7.5x to 23x), the turn-2+ payload is 1,465x to 1,600x smaller, and prompt token ids and mm hashes equal candidate-54's.

On the path the API server takes, the mark is missed, and so was it before this rework. BaseMultiModalProcessor enables its metadata cache only when getattr(self.info.ctx, 'vllm_config').cache_config.enable_prefix_caching is true, and the server's InputProcessingContext has only model_config and tokenizer. So items are never lazy and nothing is sent stripped. The PR's bench builds its own context with vllm_config, which is why it engages there. Through a real AsyncLLM frontend with the recipe's flags (fake engine core only), against candidate-54, ABBA, 2 boots each: turn 2+ sends the full ~10-41 MB every turn. 1302x1302 JPEG is 57% slower (1 image) and 35% slower (4 images), and 4032x3024 JPEG x4 is 4% slower, all beyond the interval. PNG is 5-7% faster. Step 8 counts a slower cell of the PR's own bench, on a shape serving uses, as worse.
Under the drop rule, #978 misses as a performance change on the serving path. The owner decides whether the bench result shows enough promise for a second rework (see second_rework_scope).

Not a rebase artifact: #978's own patch (PR head 67792978, sha256 f5b37879...) adds no import, and async_llm.py does not import Callable on its 1107 base (320021e3, read from the spark-ds41f:1107 image), on candidate-50, on candidate-54 (4e8133ff) or in candidate-55's 0793 (3feb241e). raw/static/static-checks.txt.
answers_to_coordinator.does_it_explain_the_13: No. Those tests replace _run_output_handler with a no-op, so they never reach the NameError. They failed on the renderer and retry-map coupling: 10 AttributeError ('AsyncLLM' object has no attribute 'renderer'), 3 TimeoutError (the send was never reached), and 3 EngineGenerateError wrapping the same AttributeError (raw/tests/gate-c55.txt).
answers_to_coordinator.import_and_real_construction: python -c 'import vllm.v1.engine.async_llm' passes on both trees; importing never triggered the error. A real AsyncLLM was constructed in a running event loop with VllmConfig from the served DS4.1 checkpoint and the recipe's --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --enable-prefix-caching --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --limit-mm-per-prompt {"image":67} --block-size 256. The real renderer, DS4.1 multimodal processor, InputProcessor and OutputProcessor were used, and only the engine-core client was an in-process fake, because one GB10 cannot load the TP4 model. Candidate-55's tree fails in __init__ with NameError: name 'Callable' is not defined, the boots' traceback. The corrected tree constructs, the output handler runs with _mm_prefix_fastpath true, and it serves a text request and a two-turn image chat through generate(); shutdown is clean (raw/construct/). The construction step expected turn 2 to go stripped and it did not, on both the corrected tree and candidate-55 with only the import fixed: that is the dormant serving path above, not a regression.
answers_to_coordinator.overlay_over_candidate_55_image: Yes, as-is. The overlay is the four files that differ between candidate-55 (410463b3) and candidate-55-r1, all Python: vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py, vllm/v1/engine/core.py and two test files. Mounted over spark-ds41f:candidate-55's /opt/spark-ds41f/candidate/vllm, they give exactly candidate-55-r1's tree (25787be1). Booting needs only the two vllm/ files. root_cause.boot: vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py, _run_output_handler: the nested `async def _retry_mm_cache_miss(retry_req: EngineCoreRequest, materializers: dict[str, Callable[[], Any]], ...)` annotates with Callable. Python 3.12 evaluates parameter annotations whenever the def runs, i.e. every time the output handler starts (AsyncLLM.__init__ in a running loop, or the first add_request). Callable was never imported, so every API server start raised NameError. All three candidate-55 boots on 2026-11-10 (04:04, 04:08 and 04:13Z) died this way (raw/candidate-55-boot/boot-failure-excerpt.txt). It is the only unbound name in candidate-55's 23 changed Python files (raw/static).
root_cause.release_tests: _add_request evaluated `self.renderer.mm_processor_cache is None and self.vllm_config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching and request.mm_features`, renderer first, for every request. abort() popped self._pending_mm_retries for every aborted id. 0723's (rollback) and 0771's (#972) tests build AsyncLLM via __new__ with the text path's attributes only, so: (a) text-only submissions raised AttributeError before the engine send. The 3 disconnect tests then timed out, because the send they wait in was never reached. The api-cancellation test got EngineGenerateError. (b) The rollback's abort() raised AttributeError after removing local state, and add_request logged it as a failed notification, so the engine abort was never sent. In production the attributes exist, so this was a coupling defect, not a serving one. The text path should not depend on multimodal state.
root_cause.engine_stripped_item: Found while reworking: vllm/v1/engine/core.py, _verify_or_resolve_stripped_mm_features did `_, num_computed_tokens = kv_cache_manager.get_computed_blocks(request)`, but this tree's get_computed_blocks returns (blocks, computed tokens, shared_prefix_boundary). The first request with a stripped item would raise ValueError in EngineCoreProc._handle_client_request, which only catches MultiModalCacheMissError, and stop the engine. #978's test stub returned a 2-tuple and hid it.
root_cause.await_window: The materialization await sits between output_processor.add_request (local registration) and engine_core.add_request_async, inside add_request()'s `except BaseException` rollback (0723) and before abort()'s shielded engine notification (0771/#972). Structurally it keeps #972's guarantees: cancellation or failure there rolls back the registration and every registered child, and the abort is shielded. Two leaks remained. A request whose send failed left its new identifiers in _p1_cached_mm_identifiers. A cache-miss retry whose request was aborted during its materialization was resubmitted anyway, as an engine request with no client, and its items were re-marked.

vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py: class attribute _mm_prefix_fastpath = False; __init__ sets it once: renderer.mm_processor is not None and renderer.mm_processor_cache is None and cache_config.enable_prefix_caching (the renderer's cache is fixed at construction)

_add_request: `if request.mm_features and self._mm_prefix_fastpath:` (text-only requests check one request attribute and never reach the renderer or the fast path); the await stays inside add_request()'s rollback
_prepare_mm_features_for_prefix_cache returns the identifiers it newly marked (deduplicated, not already present); its effects are otherwise unchanged, so the PR's bench still drives it directly

the engine send is wrapped: if it raises or is cancelled, a fast-path request drops its retry entry and unmarks the identifiers it marked (a request whose send did not complete leaves no fast-path state)
abort(): the retry-map cleanup runs only when the fast path is on and the map is not empty; still before the shielded abort
_retry_mm_cache_miss: after materializing, if output_processor no longer has the request (aborted meanwhile), return without re-marking or resubmitting
tests/multimodal/test_prefix_cache_fastp: the get_computed_blocks stub returns the real 3 values, and the test asserts KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks' return annotation has 3 elements with int at index 1

fix.marks_semantics: An identifier is marked as sent to P1 only by a request whose engine send completed. A request rolled back before its send completed unmarks what it marked. Marks made by a delivered request stay, as after any ordinary abort: an earlier turn, or an earlier sampled child of the same submission whose send completed before a later child failed. P1 verifies every stripped item (encoder cache, prefix coverage, another request's data) and otherwise returns a retryable miss.

residual_risks_not_fixed: The fast path is dormant in serving (above). Enabling it means telling the processor that prefix caching is on: the renderer knows (config.cache_config), and InputProcessingContext does not carry it. Doing that would put stripped requests into serving for the first time.

If stripped items were ever sent: the engine accepts a stripped item that is only covered by the prefix cache, without a pin. If those blocks are evicted before the request is scheduled, or the request is preempted and its encoder entry is evicted, the scheduler can only borrow the data from another live request. Otherwise it schedules the encoder with data None, and the worker raises 'Encoder cache miss' (gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py), stopping the engine. A schedule-time retryable miss is needed before this path can serve.
n>1 with stripped items: sampled children share mm_features (shallow copy). Only the first child keeps a retry materializer, so a P1 miss on a later child finishes it with an error.
_p1_cached_mm_identifiers is unbounded (one entry per distinct image until a reset).
A cache-miss retry materializes inline in the output handler, which stalls all requests' outputs for that time.
A cancelled materialization keeps running on the single-worker MM executor until its batch ends.
getattr(self.scheduler, 'ced_Prompt_replay_tokens', 0) names no attribute, so it is dead code; get_computed_blocks already caps the hit at the replay boundary.
second_rework_scope: Only if the owner sees promise: (1) the renderer tells the processor that prefix caching is on; (2) a schedule-time retryable miss (or a pin) for stripped items whose coverage is lost; (3) find the frontend JPEG slowdown (header cache and _LazyPILImage path); (4) judge on serving_path_bench.py against candidate-54, ABBA, plus check_978_image_chat.py at tp4-ring.
